meta.definition: The Detail Department's recommendation for real daily AI paid-media work today, scored against the human job for each category rather than one universal feature checklist.

statusDefinition.Production: Dependable enough for a controlled recurring workflow today.
statusDefinition.Test: Worth piloting, but access, maturity or control needs a bounded test.
statusDefinition.Research: Useful specialist capability, not a daily operating interface.

positives: Official, maintained MCP with a clear read boundary.
Google Ads Query Language supports detailed account and performance diagnosis.
Useful as a reporting and second-pair-of-eyes surface once configured.
negatives: The MCP cannot create, modify or delete any campaign object.
Setup requires Python, a developer token, Google Cloud, enabled APIs, OAuth and client configuration.
The workflow stops at diagnosis and cannot perform the optimisation it recommends.

positives: Hosted OAuth makes the connector much easier to add than a custom Marketing API integration.
It can read performance and campaign structure in the assistant.
It can create supported campaign, ad-set and ad objects.
negatives: The current beta does not provide dependable general modification of existing campaign objects.
Availability still varies by ad account and by individual tool.
Creation without ordinary follow-up editing sends the operator back to Ads Manager.

positives: Official remote MCP covers campaign, reporting, audience and creative work.
Read/write capability makes it useful beyond analysis.
The interface is designed for advertiser workflows rather than a generic API bridge.
negatives: Broad write permissions increase the cost of a bad instruction.
Business account eligibility and permissions still govern availability.
No dedicated official CLI was verified.

positives: Official managed connection is easier than building against the API.
Provides entity-level performance data for campaigns, ad groups, ads and keywords.
Useful for conversational audits and cross-platform reporting.
negatives: The documented launch surface is read-only.
It cannot create an ad or apply the campaign changes suggested by an audit.
Broad manage-campaign language on the product page overstates the action boundary described in its FAQ.

positives: Official MCP can create, update and delete campaign objects.
Retail-media context makes it strategically important.
Uses the established Amazon Ads API permission model.
negatives: The MCP is still an open beta.
Access is limited to partners with active API credentials.
Destructive campaign operations require strong human approval gates.

positives: Official hosted MCP provides campaign retrieval and analysis.
Read-only control is suitable for a cautious reporting pilot.
The underlying Marketing API offers a route to deeper integration.
negatives: MCP access is still allowlisted.
The MCP cannot execute campaign changes.
No official plugin or dedicated CLI was verified.

positives: Official Marketing APIs cover campaign management and reporting.
Strong fit for B2B audience and lead-generation workflows.
Production access tiers and permissions are documented.
negatives: No official MCP was verified.
API product approval and access tiers add friction.
Daily AI use needs a custom or third-party integration layer.

positives: Official Ads API supports campaign and reporting workflows.
Useful specialist channel for visual discovery and commerce.
An authorised integration can run recurring production tasks.
negatives: No official MCP or agent plugin was verified.
No dedicated official CLI was verified.
AI workflows require custom engineering or a maintained intermediary.

positives: Official Ads API v3 exposes campaign and account operations.
Community context can be valuable for specific audience strategies.
OAuth provides a conventional route for controlled integrations.
negatives: No official MCP, plugin or CLI was verified.
Advertising API access requires approval.
A useful daily agent workflow must be built and maintained separately.

positives: Official Ads-specific MCP documents campaign and line-item writes.
New campaigns and line items start paused, with separate activation tools.
Includes targeting, creative, audience and conversion-tracking tools.
negatives: Developer-app and Ads access remain prerequisites.
Campaign deletion is not in the documented MCP tool list.
Activation and budget changes require explicit operating controls.

positives: Mature official API covers core programmatic campaign resources.
Supports insertion orders, line items, targeting, creatives and users.
Role-based access can separate read, standard and admin operations.
negatives: No official MCP or agent plugin was verified.
Performance reporting requires the separate Bid Manager API.
Some YouTube and Partners write workflows remain outside the API.

positives: Mature API supports trafficking, creative, conversion and reporting workflows.
Broad resource coverage suits complex enterprise operations.
User-profile permissions remain the control plane.
negatives: No official MCP, plugin or dedicated CLI was verified.
The resource model and permissions create implementation overhead.
Write access can affect live trafficking and needs a second-person check.

positives: High-volume official reporting API with a purpose-built query language.
Immediate access to granular campaign, ad and keyword data.
REST, gRPC and official client libraries support production pipelines.
negatives: The reporting API is read-only.
Offline conversions use a separate API surface.
No official MCP or dedicated agent integration was verified.

positives: Official API supports campaign, ad-group, keyword and reporting work.
API roles distinguish read-only from read/write access.
Covers ads on the App Store and Apple Maps.
negatives: No official MCP, plugin or dedicated CLI was verified.
Third-party providers require separate registration.
Daily AI use needs a custom integration and careful OAuth setup.

positives: Official OAK MCP connects AI assistants to Ask Koa.
Published scope includes querying data, creating campaigns and monitoring live activity.
The underlying REST and GraphQL APIs cover substantial platform operations.
negatives: OAK is available only to selected partners in private beta.
Broad action scope makes approval and audit controls essential.
Practical onboarding still depends on an account representative.

positives: Official open-source MCP is suitable for recurring reporting and analysis.
Read-only design limits accidental property changes.
Google Analytics data and administration APIs provide a mature foundation.
negatives: The MCP cannot edit events, audiences or property settings.
Cloud credentials and property permissions still require setup.
No separate official plugin or marketer-facing CLI was verified.

positives: Official API supports container, workspace, tag, trigger and variable workflows.
Useful for repeatable measurement deployment and governance.
Workspace and version concepts support controlled changes.
negatives: No official MCP, agent plugin or dedicated CLI was verified.
Incorrect writes can damage live measurement.
Safe automation needs preview, review and publication gates outside the API.

positives: Official MCP supports both analysis and write operations.
Official agent plugins, skills and a CLI create several usable entry points.
Strong fit for behavioural analysis and experimentation workflows.
negatives: Write capability requires careful project and taxonomy governance.
It is an analytics layer, not a media-buying control plane.
Teams still need consistent event instrumentation for useful answers.

positives: The official tool reference now documents dashboard creation, updates and deletion.
Lexicon editing and data-quality tools extend the route beyond reporting.
Regional endpoints and OAuth or service-account authentication are documented.
negatives: Experiments, feature flags and audit-log tools have beta or access limits.
Free-plan query limits and organisation enablement can affect availability.
Documented tools still need a controlled account-level pilot.

positives: Official read-only MCP fits recurring cross-channel retrieval.
Established connector coverage reduces bespoke API maintenance.
Official AI integrations and CLI provide several workflow options.
negatives: The CLI remains alpha.
The MCP cannot change campaigns.
Coverage and economics depend on the commercial plan and connector.

positives: Official MCP and CLI make search and competitive data directly usable by agents.
Read-only control is appropriate for external research data.
Broad API coverage supports repeatable market and SERP analysis.
negatives: It does not operate advertising accounts.
Usage-based API costs need monitoring.
Raw results still require paid-media judgement before action.

positives: Official agent MCP can expose useful connector and data-movement context.
Large connector ecosystem supports cross-channel data collection.
Open-source and managed routes give teams deployment choice.
negatives: MCP control is mixed and depends on the configured interface.
Self-hosting adds operational overhead.
It is infrastructure rather than a marketer-facing daily interface.

positives: Mature managed data movement supports reliable recurring pipelines.
Official MCP, agent plugins and Connector SDK CLI cover several technical workflows.
Read-only MCP control is a sensible context boundary.
negatives: Agent Context MCP is still a public preview.
The MCP is not a substitute for connector operations or warehouse permissions.
Enterprise cost and administration may be disproportionate for a small stack.

positives: Official open-source toolbox exposes governed database tools through MCP.
Supports BigQuery and other common production data stores.
CLI and Gemini extensions help teams package repeatable access.
negatives: It is not a paid-media connector by itself.
Read/write risk depends entirely on tool definitions and database roles.
Secure configuration requires data-engineering discipline.

positives: Official managed MCP works inside Snowflake's role and governance model.
Strong foundation for cross-channel measurement and governed client data.
Official CLI, APIs and drivers support serious production engineering.
negatives: It needs warehouse, role and cost governance expertise.
Mixed control can expose consequential writes when roles are too broad.
It is infrastructure, not a ready-made paid-media workflow.

positives: Google-backed open-source marketing-mix modelling package.
Useful for incrementality and budget-allocation questions beyond platform attribution.
Python package can be made reproducible in a governed modelling workflow.
negatives: No official MCP, plugin or dedicated CLI was verified.
Requires statistical skill and suitable historical data.
It is not a daily campaign-operation interface.

positives: Established open-source marketing-mix modelling project from Meta.
Supports automated model exploration and budget-allocation analysis.
R and Python routes broaden analyst access.
negatives: No official MCP or marketer-facing CLI was verified.
Model selection and calibration still require specialist judgement.
Outputs do not translate directly into safe platform changes.

positives: Flexible Bayesian tooling for media-mix and customer-value modelling.
Open source and inspectable for teams that need methodological control.
Python ecosystem supports custom analysis and reproducibility.
negatives: Requires strong Python and statistical expertise.
No official MCP, plugin or dedicated workflow CLI was verified.
It is a modelling library rather than a daily media-operations product.

positives: Official MCP reaches a broad catalogue of business applications.
Read/write actions make it useful for practical cross-tool workflows.
Platform CLI supports maintained custom integrations.
negatives: Connector depth and field coverage vary by application.
Broad action access can create unintended external changes.
Task limits and commercial plans can constrain high-volume operations.

positives: Official MCP and CLI support flexible API-based automation.
Code steps handle gaps that fixed connectors cannot cover.
Strong fit for event-driven media and measurement workflows.
negatives: More engineering-oriented than a typical marketer tool.
Credential and secret handling needs careful ownership.
Failures can cross several connected systems and need monitoring.

positives: The instance MCP documents workflow creation and editing as well as execution.
Workflow enablement and user permissions bound access.
Self-hosting supports teams that can own the operational setup.
negatives: Building and editing require n8n 2.13.0 or later.
Enabled workflow access is shared across connected clients rather than separately selected per client.
Workflow execution can trigger external writes using connected credentials.

positives: Official remote and desktop MCP expose real design context.
Supported clients can create or modify native canvas content.
Plugin API and agent skills support structured creative workflows.
negatives: Write-to-canvas is beta and depends on current seat eligibility and file permissions.
It does not connect creative output to media-platform delivery by itself.
No dedicated official Figma CLI was verified.

positives: Official MCP supports design creation, editing, assets and export.
Remote OAuth makes it accessible to common agent clients.
Apps CLI and Connect APIs support deeper product integration.
negatives: The Apps CLI is not a daily creative-production CLI.
Brand and format governance still need human review.
It does not validate media-platform setup or campaign delivery.

positives: Hosted official MCP with normal Adobe permissions.
Creates and runs ranked or trended reports.
Can manage segments, date ranges and workspace projects.
negatives: Enterprise entitlement and administrator permissions are required.
It does not operate ad platforms.
Report correctness still depends on governed suites and components.

positives: Official hosted MCP for cross-channel analysis.
Uses the organisation existing CJA permissions.
Can work with reusable components and projects.
negatives: Useful only after substantial data-view and identity work.
Enterprise access raises the setup bar.
It cannot repair upstream instrumentation.

positives: Queries the major product-analytics methods and SQL.
Creates, updates and deletes insights and dashboards.
One-command wizard installation is unusually direct.
negatives: It is product-led rather than paid-media-led.
Quality depends on the event implementation.
It does not control media spend or delivery.

positives: Hosted official MCP with OAuth and token routes.
Useful campaign and attribution diagnosis in chat.
Includes implementation and OneLink troubleshooting.
negatives: The service is explicitly beta.
Sessions can require frequent reconnection.
The reviewed route diagnoses more than it configures.

positives: Mature APIs and SDKs cover measurement and reporting.
App Automation can create or update configured apps.
Device APIs support testing workflows.
negatives: No official MCP or agent plugin was verified.
Capabilities are split across several APIs.
Some automation requires vendor enablement.

positives: Mature collection and routing infrastructure.
Public API provides CRUD for core workspace resources.
Strong governance surface for tracking plans and destinations.
negatives: No official MCP was verified.
A custom agent layer is required.
Identity and instrumentation design remain specialist work.

positives: Hosted MCP runs real reusable creative workflows.
Supports generation, editing, composition and format variants.
Asynchronous monitoring fits large production jobs.
negatives: Enterprise-only access limits practical adoption.
Workflow design must exist before reliable reuse.
Human brand and output review remains essential.

positives: Official MCP, API, SDKs and open GitHub server.
Creates and edits image, video and audio assets.
Task APIs and reusable workflows support automation.
negatives: Outputs still need rights and brand review.
Temporary result URLs require disciplined download.
Generation cost and model choice need controls.

positives: Hosted official MCP with straightforward OAuth.
Strong keyword, backlink and competitor evidence.
Useful without building a custom API wrapper.
negatives: Read-only research rather than activation.
Requires an eligible paid plan.
It does not include first-party campaign truth.

positives: Hosted OAuth endpoint works across major clients.
Broad SEO, paid-search, shopping and market reports.
Discovery tools make a large API easier for agents.
negatives: Every call consumes API units.
Project methods exposed by MCP are read-only.
Subscription entitlements make coverage variable.

positives: Hosted MCP covers more than 75 intelligence endpoints.
Strong web, app, search, audience and retail breadth.
Supports direct competitor comparison.
negatives: Requires API-inclusive paid access.
Queries consume data credits.
Estimated and delayed datasets are not first-party live truth.

positives: Hosted OAuth MCP is easy to connect.
Can access and manage sources, destinations and transformations.
Covers event streams and documentation.
negatives: Official docs warn that the MCP is still in active development.
Some product features are missing.
Connection stability may vary during updates.

positives: Managed MCP uses workspace governance and permissions.
Can expose SQL, Genie and Vector Search.
Strong fit for governed enterprise data estates.
negatives: Managed MCP remains public preview.
Requires substantial platform configuration.
Not a turn-key paid-media connection.

positives: Official open-source MCP with broad toolsets.
Strong lineage, health, semantic and SQL context.
Can run build and test when explicitly enabled.
negatives: Setup changes materially by toolset.
Useful operation requires analytics-engineering expertise.
CLI writes can change warehouse objects.

positives: Universal hosted OAuth endpoint.
Can run scenarios on all plans.
Paid scopes can manage scenarios and related entities.
negatives: Scenario quality depends on clear inputs and outputs.
Management scopes can affect live automation.
Connector depth still varies by app.

positives: Enterprise-hosted runtime with identity and audit controls.
Exposes recipes, API collections, functions and skills.
Strong governance for consequential workflows.
negatives: Enterprise-only access.
An administrator must create the endpoint.
Setup is heavier than self-service competitors.

positives: AI-native agent and workflow construction.
Supports 50-plus built-in and arbitrary remote MCP servers.
CLI has JSON output for automation.
negatives: No universal external Gumloop MCP endpoint was verified.
Production reliability inherits every connected dependency.
External MCP servers must be publicly reachable.
